title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
lead: An exponential function has a constant base and a variable exponent. Here such functions are evaluated, graphed and set against power functions; the number e comes out of compound interest; logarithms are taken as their inverses and used to solve equations in any base; and the hyperbolic functions are built from ex and e−x.
objectives: Identify the form of an exponential function.
Explain the difference between the graphs of $x^{b}$ and $b^{x}.$
Recognize the significance of the number $e.$
Identify the form of a logarithmic function.
Explain the relationship between exponential and logarithmic functions.
Describe how to calculate a logarithm to a different base.
Identify the hyperbolic functions, their graphs, and basic identities.
summary_html:
• The exponential function $y=b^{x}$ is increasing if $b\gt 1$ and decreasing if $0\lt b\lt 1.$ Its domain is $(-\infty,\infty)$ and its range is $(0,\infty).$
  • The logarithmic function $y=\log_{b}(x)$ is the inverse of $y=b^{x}.$ Its domain is $(0,\infty)$ and its range is $(-\infty,\infty).$
  • The natural exponential function is $y=e^{x}$ and the natural logarithmic function is $y=\ln x=\log_{e}x.$
  • Given an exponential function or logarithmic function in base $a,$ we can make a change of base to convert this function to any base $b\gt 0,b\ne 1.$ We typically convert to base $e.$
  • The hyperbolic functions involve combinations of the exponential functions $e^{x}$ and $e^{-x}.$ As a result, the inverse hyperbolic functions involve the natural logarithm.

[T] The number of bacteria N in a culture after t days can be modeled by the function $N(t)=1300\cdot (2)^{t/4}.$ Find the number of bacteria present after 15 days.
[T] The amount A of a ＄100,000 investment paying continuously and compounded for t years is given by $A(t)=100,000\cdot e^{0.055t}.$ Find the amount A accumulated in 5 years.

[T] The concentration of hydrogen ions in a substance is denoted by $[\text{H}^{+}],$ measured in moles per liter. The pH of a substance is defined by the logarithmic function $\text{pH}=-\log[\text{H}^{+}].$ This function is used to measure the acidity of a substance. The pH of water is 7. A substance with a pH less than 7 is an acid, whereas one that has a pH of more than 7 is a base.

a. Find the pH of the following substances. Round answers to one digit.

b. Determine whether the substance is an acid or a base.

  1. Eggs: $[\text{H}^{+}]=1.6\times 10^{-8}$ mol/L
  2. Beer: $[\text{H}^{+}]=3.16\times 10^{-3}$ mol/L
  3. Tomato Juice: $[\text{H}^{+}]=7.94\times 10^{-5}$ mol/L

answer.solution: i. a. pH = 8 b. Base ii. a. pH = 3 b. Acid iii. a. pH = 4 b. Acid

steps.cap: Each year multiplies the amount by $1+r$, so after $t$ years it has been multiplied by $1+r$ a total of $t$ times.

assumes.text: Compounded twice a year, each half year adds interest of $\frac{r}{2}$ times the amount held at its start.

steps.cap: Each year holds two half years, so after $t$ years the amount has been multiplied by $1+\frac{r}{2}$ a total of $2t$ times.
Compounded $n$ times a year, each period multiplies the amount by $1+\frac{r}{n}$, as each year multiplied it by $1+r$ and each half year by $1+\frac{r}{2}$; $t$ years hold $nt$ periods.

The two roots multiply to $\frac{x}{x}=1$, so the one with the minus sign is at most $1$, while $y\ge 0$ makes $e^{y}\ge e^{0}=1$.
A quadratic equation in $e^{y}$, with $a=x$, $b=-2$ and $c=-x$; $x\ne 0$, as $x$ is $2$ over a difference.
As $\sqrt{1+x^{2}}\gt 1$, $e^{y}\gt 0$ takes the plus sign when $x\gt 0$ and the minus sign when $x\lt 0$. Both are $\frac{1}{x}+\frac{\sqrt{1+x^{2}}}{|x|}$.
